title: K5 common-order mixed covariance finite-part metric ambiguity audit
scope: Linearized Gaussian K5 surrogate only. Iter421 established a universal eta^-6 exponent under generic cut/cycle mixing with one common cycle scaling order. Iter422 tests whether the renormalized finite coefficient is itself unique or retains seed-metric dependence.
construction: Use the same orthonormal K5 cut/cycle split Q=[Qc,Qz] and full SPD seed H as Iter421, with Sigma_eta = Q D_eta H D_eta Q^T and D_eta=diag(I_4, eta I_6). Define R_H(eta)=eta^6 exp[-0.5 log det Sigma_eta]. Since det(Q)^2=1 and det(D_eta)^2=eta^12, the exact prediction is R_H = det(H)^(-1/2), independent of eta but dependent on H. A determinant-normalized control Hbar=H/det(H)^(1/10) must give R_Hbar=1.

frozen_predictions.interpretation: common spectral order fixes the divergence exponent but not the finite normalization unless the microscopic prescription also fixes the regulator metric volume

profile_variation: 24 deterministic full-SPD seeds spanning weak through strong cut-cycle mixing and multiple conditioning regimes. No gate tuning after results.
claim_lock: A PASS establishes finite-part non-universality only inside this linearized Gaussian regulator class. It does not identify the physical EPRL/Toller regulator metric, does not prove the true spin-foam vertex is ambiguous, and does not close D7 or NEW_REQUIRED.
